flawed_step: Writing P(S|T) = P(S|T,C)P(C|T) + P(S|T,¬C)P(¬C|T) and P(S|¬T) = P(S|¬T,C)P(C|¬T) + P(S|¬T,¬C)P(¬C|¬T), concluding P(S|T) > P(S|¬T) needs the same weights, P(C|T) = P(C|¬T). The hypotheses don't give this, so the comparison step cannot be justified (Simpson's paradox).
counterexample: Uniform space of 700 outcomes. T∩C: 87 outcomes, 81 in S. ¬T∩C: 270 outcomes, 234 in S. T∩¬C: 263 outcomes, 192 in S. ¬T∩¬C: 80 outcomes, 55 in S. Stratum C: 81/87 > 234/270, since 21870 > 20358. Stratum ¬C: 192/263 > 55/80, since 15360 > 14465. Overall: P(S|T) = 273/350 = 0.78 < P(S|¬T) = 289/350 ≈ 0.826. All four cells have positive probability.
assessment_summary: The statement is false; it is Simpson's paradox. Each overall rate is a weighted average of its stratum rates, and the weights P(C|T) and P(C|¬T) can differ. The explicit counterexample above (the kidney-stone numbers) has T better in both strata but worse overall, and all the inequalities were checked by cross-multiplication.
